QUESTION: Given a mapping $M$ specified by a set of st-tgds, how does the algorithm Inverse construct a maximum recovery of $M$? Describe what it does for each st-tgd $\phi(\bar x) \to \exists \bar y\, \psi(\bar x,\bar y)$.

ATOM: For a mapping $M$ specified by st-tgds, the algorithm Inverse builds a maximum recovery by taking, for each st-tgd $\phi(\bar x) \to \exists \bar y\, \psi(\bar x,\bar y)$, a UCQ$^=$ source rewriting $\alpha(\bar x)$ of the query $\exists \bar y\, \psi(\bar x,\bar y)$ and adding the dependency $\exists \bar y\, \psi(\bar x,\bar y) \wedge C(\bar x) \to \alpha(\bar x)$.
KEY POINTS:
1. Compute a source rewriting $\alpha(\bar x)$ in UCQ$^=$ of the conjunctive query $\exists \bar y\, \psi(\bar x,\bar y)$
2. Add the dependency $\exists \bar y\, \psi(\bar x,\bar y) \wedge C(\bar x) \to \alpha(\bar x)$

ANSWER TO GRADE:
For each st-tgd, Inverse decomposes the target conjunction into components connected by existential variables and forms a target query for each component. It rewrites each query into a disjunction of its possible source-side causes under all the st-tgds, then adds an inverse implication from the target query to that source condition, restricting distinguished source values to constants.
